instructions.primary_message: This recipe makes about 12 cups of loosely packed pilaf or 8 (1 ½ cup) servings.
Preheat a large pot over medium heat.
While the pot heats up, using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and set aside.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add orzo and cook; stirring occasionally, until golden, 3-4 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
¾ cup orzo pasta

instructions.primary_message: When the orzo is toasted, add garlic to the pot. Continue to cook, while stirring, until garlic is fragrant, 1 minute.

Add drained rice, broth, salt, and pepper to the pot, then bring the mixture to a boil over high heat. Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the pot, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice and orzo until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove pilaf from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
5 ½ cups mushroom broth
¾ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message:
STORING: When the rice is done, fluff with a fork. Divide between 2 large baking sheet pans, spreading the pilaf out in an even layer. Let cool to room temperature, about 30 minutes. Once cool, use clean hands to separate the grains (if needed), then divide pilaf between containers with lids or resealable plastic bags (gently pressing out extra air if using bags). Store in the freezer for up to 2 months. 



HEATING: Preheat oven to 350°F. While the oven heats up, set rice pilaf on the counter to thaw slightly. When the oven is heated, transfer frozen rice pilaf to a baking sheet pan, breaking it up into smaller pieces. Bake in the oven, stirring halfway, until heated through, 20-25 minutes. Alternatively, place rice in a lightly oiled skillet, cover with a lid, and cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until heated through, 8-10 minutes. (You may need to break up larger chunks with a spoon.)
